source: Native AWS captures; retained consumer documents, not emulator-generated expectations
normalization: Only account 123456789012 is replaced with 123456789012 in retained requests and documents. Capture indexes identify zero-based observations/calls. Runtime replay uses the account returned by its IAM role API and Python 3.12 instead of the metric capture Python 3.13.
limitations: No automatic CLI retries or pagination. Explicit recovery recreated the same role three times and same Lambda/alarm/rule/queue identities twice after deletion; never more than one of each existed concurrently. Transport failures are not AWS semantic evidence.
No PutMetricData calls; zero intentional retained custom metric points. Lambda publishes normal AWS service metrics, which have no deletion API.

Negative action observations are bounded windows, not a universal proof about arbitrarily delayed delivery. Final alarm history contains one missing-permission failure and two intended successes. Collected log pages contain two unique handler events.
Observed SQS receive order was not alarm transition order; consumers must not assume ordering or exactly-once delivery from this sample.
Alarm history includes initial recovered creation/deletion and final workflow because CloudWatch retained history across deleting and recreating the same alarm name.
Only same-account unqualified Python Lambda actions tested; wrong-source policies, qualified aliases/versions, cross-account delivery, Lambda handler errors and retry behavior not exercised.
All absence verifications succeeded; an API not-found result in cleanup verification is expected evidence of absence rather than failed cleanup.

The final unpaginated FilterLogEvents request returned an empty page with nextToken, despite earlier requests capturing both real handler events. No pagination was performed, as required; use logs_enabled_ok and logs_enabled_alarm as invocation payload evidence, not final_lambda_logs. Log capture is not an exhaustive stream inventory.
Composite source EventBridge rule selected state changes only, so this fixture does not claim composite configuration-event evidence.
Composite handler records are actual FilterLogEvents stdout payloads. WaitPeriod and ExtensionPeriod release retained equal ALARM values with suppression phase in previousState.
Native wall-clock receive order/latency is not a scheduling guarantee. Replay separates one-second composite notification ticks from independent configured five-second suppression deadlines.

Comparisons preserve field presence, JSON-string reasonData and parsed structured data; generated prose, opaque IDs, and absolute wall-clock timestamps are not golden strings. Timestamp equality/order is checked per semantic field, without equating child mutation time with delayed composite processing time.
Action failure prose is retained as evidence but compared as a nonempty error, not a stable AWS wording contract. Action timestamp relations and null fields remain significant.
